word:hebrew:H1008.explanation: Beth-El is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H1044.explanation: Beth-Eked is a place name referring to a shearing house.

word:hebrew:H1101.explanation: Bâlal means to mix or mingle. It can describe fine flour mixed with oil.

word:hebrew:H1282.explanation: Bariah is a Hebrew personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. In the Old Testament Hebrew text, it occurs once, in 1 Chronicles 3:22, and is rendered “Bariah.” Because the available information identifies it only as a name and does not provide an explicit definition, its meaning cannot be expanded beyond that proper-name function. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain the person’s role in that passage.

word:hebrew:H1376.explanation: Gebir means a master or lord, a person who has authority over others.

word:hebrew:H1398.explanation: This word refers to “Geber,” a personal name rather than a general description or action. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 1 Kings 4:19, and the English rendering preserves it as a name. Because it functions as a name, its basic meaning is to identify a particular person; the surrounding verse is needed to explain that person’s role in the passage. The word itself does not provide a broader common meaning in the available record.

word:hebrew:H1453.explanation: In the Hebrew Old Testament, this word refers to “Gederothaim,” a named designation rather than a general descriptive term. It occurs once, in Joshua 15:36, and the English rendering preserves it as a name. Because no explicit definition or surrounding verse text is available here, its precise referent cannot be described more narrowly from the word alone. Its role is therefore chiefly identifying: it singles out Gederothaim wherever this one occurrence is read.

word:hebrew:H1505.explanation: Gᵉzar means to quarry or cut out. It can also refer to a soothsayer.

word:hebrew:H151.explanation: Adoram is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H1642.explanation: Gerar is the name of a Philistine city.

word:hebrew:H1714.explanation: Degel means a flag, banner, or standard.

word:hebrew:H1758.explanation: Dush means to trample or thresh.

word:hebrew:H2056.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a child. It functions as a noun naming a young person, rather than describing an action or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Genesis 11:30, and is rendered “child” in both recorded English renderings. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context, but the word itself carries this straightforward meaning.

word:hebrew:H216.explanation: Or means light or illumination. It can also refer to lightning.

word:hebrew:H2175.explanation: Zimran is a personal name, referring to a man named Zimran in the Hebrew Scriptures. The name appears twice in the Old Testament corpus, both times in genealogical passages that record family descent. It is associated with birth or begetting and functions as the name of an individual rather than a general description or action. Its occurrences are Genesis 25:2 and 1 Chronicles 1:32.

word:hebrew:H2229.explanation: Zaram means to gush like water, as clouds pour out water. It can also describe being carried away as with a flood.

word:hebrew:H2250.explanation: Chabburah means a bruise, wound, or stripe.

word:hebrew:H2391.explanation: The Hebrew word means “strength,” referring to power, firmness, or capacity to withstand. Its central idea is strong support or might rather than weakness. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Psalm 18:1, so its broader range of use cannot be established from repeated occurrences. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain its precise force there, but “strength” is the supported ordinary meaning.

word:hebrew:H2500.explanation: This Hebrew word is a rare term whose precise meaning cannot be stated confidently from the lexical information available here. It occurs only twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Numbers 18:21 and 18:31. The word’s identity is preserved, but no explicit definition, gloss, or approved meaning clue accompanies it. Its exact sense therefore requires examination of the verse text and surrounding passage rather than a broader lexical claim.

word:hebrew:H2579.explanation: Chamath-Rabbah is the name of Hamath the great.

word:hebrew:H2661.explanation: Chaphor refers to a burrowing animal, probably a rat or mole.

word:hebrew:H2683.explanation: Chêtsen means the bosom, the area between the arms.

word:hebrew:H2728.explanation: This Hebrew word means “beetle.” It is a noun used as the name of a particular creature rather than as an action, quality, or description. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Leviticus 11:22. Since the available lexical support identifies it simply as “beetle,” that is the clearest ordinary meaning without adding a more specific identification. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and its treatment of the named creature.

word:hebrew:H2764.explanation: Cherem means a devoted thing. It can also describe something appointed for destruction.

word:hebrew:H2841.explanation: Chashrah means a gathering of watery clouds. It is rendered as “dark” alongside waters and thick clouds.

word:hebrew:H2984.explanation: “Ibhar” is a Hebrew personal name, functioning as the name of an individual rather than as a common word describing an action, object, or quality. It appears three times in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, and each occurrence is rendered “Ibhar.” The name occurs in passages recording David’s sons. No additional ordinary meaning is established for this name in the available lexical material.

word:hebrew:H3077.explanation: Jehoiada is a personal name. In one passage, Jehoiada is named as Benaiah’s father; in another, Jehoiada is called a priest.

word:hebrew:H3118.explanation: Yom means a day and can also mean time.

word:hebrew:H3154.explanation: This Hebrew word means “sweat,” referring to bodily moisture. It names a physical substance rather than an action, person, or place. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs once, in Ezekiel 44:18. Since the word appears only once and the verse text is not provided here, its basic lexical meaning can be stated clearly, while its precise force in that passage depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H3213.explanation: Yâlal means to howl, especially with a wailing tone.

word:hebrew:H3309.explanation: This Hebrew word functions as a proper name, rendered "Japhia." It identifies named individuals or a named location rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The word occurs five times in the Hebrew Old Testament, appearing in Joshua, Samuel, and Chronicles. Its precise referent—whether a person or place—depends on the surrounding verse, but its normal lexical role is to designate someone or somewhere by name.

word:hebrew:H3370.explanation: Jokshan is a personal name, rendered “Jokshan.” It identifies a person in the genealogical records of Genesis and 1 Chronicles rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The name appears four times in the Hebrew Old Testament, across three verses. Its recorded relationships place it within birth and family lineage statements, helping readers recognize it as an individual named in the ancestry of Abraham’s family. The precise role in any particular verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H3406.explanation: Jerimoth, also rendered “Jeremoth,” is a personal name used for several individuals in the Old Testament. It does not function here as a general word describing an object, action, or quality. The name appears 15 times across 14 Old Testament verses, especially in genealogical and historical lists. Because the same name is associated with more than one person, the surrounding passage is needed to identify which Jerimoth or Jeremoth is intended in a particular verse.

word:hebrew:H3543.explanation: Kâhâh means to grow dull or become dim, especially of the eyes. It can also mean to fail.

word:hebrew:H3631.explanation: This Hebrew word means “failing.” It functions as a noun, naming a condition rather than describing an action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs twice: once in Deuteronomy 28:65 and once in Isaiah 10:22. The same central sense is represented in both occurrences, so the word consistently points to failing as a condition. Its precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning remains stable.

word:hebrew:H3792.explanation: Kethab means writing or something written. It can also mean prescribing.

word:hebrew:H3833.explanation: Lābî means a lion. It can also refer to a lioness or a young lion.

word:hebrew:H3910.explanation: Lôṭ means a sticky gum, probably ladanum, rendered as myrrh.

word:hebrew:H3969.explanation: Me'ah means a hundred, or one hundred.

word:hebrew:H4043.explanation: Magen means a shield or buckler. Figuratively, it can describe a protector, as Yahweh is called a shield around the speaker.

word:hebrew:H4106.explanation: Mahir means quick or skillful. It can also describe someone ready and diligent in work.

word:hebrew:H4292.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “besom,” a sweeping implement used to clear away dirt or debris. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Isaiah 14:23, so it is a rare, concrete word rather than a term used broadly for ideas, actions, or character. It names the tool itself; the surrounding passage is needed to determine the significance of its use in that verse.

word:hebrew:H4331.explanation: In the Hebrew Old Testament, this word is a personal name rendered “Mesha.” It appears once, at 1 Chronicles 8:9, so it identifies a named individual rather than expressing a general idea or action. Its recorded use belongs to a genealogical setting, where the name is connected with a birth or begetting relationship. Because the surrounding verse text is not included here, the person’s specific identity and role should be taken from that passage rather than inferred from the name itself.

word:hebrew:H4418.explanation: Malach means a rag or old garment, including a rotten rag.

word:hebrew:H4454.explanation: This Hebrew word functions as “it,” pointing to a thing already understood in the sentence rather than naming that thing again. It occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Leviticus: Leviticus 1:15 and 5:8. Because no explicit definition is available here, its clearest supported meaning is this pronoun-like reference. Its precise role in each verse depends on the surrounding wording, but it consistently identifies the object under discussion.

word:hebrew:H4502.explanation: This Hebrew word means “crowned,” referring to someone or something marked by a crown. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Nahum 3:17, and functions there as the object of the sentence. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain its specific reference in that passage, but its basic sense remains centered on being crowned. Its related scriptural connections also treat it as something associated with other actions concerning the same subject.

word:hebrew:H4577.explanation: Me'ah means the belly, or the bowels.

word:hebrew:H4609.explanation: Maʻălâh refers to an ascent or elevation. It can also name a step or stairway.

word:hebrew:H4670.explanation: Miphtan means a threshold or sill.

word:hebrew:H4713.explanation: Mitsrîy means an Egyptian, an inhabitant of Egypt.

word:hebrew:H4865.explanation: Mishbetsah means a setting for a gem, a holder that encloses the stone.

word:hebrew:H487.explanation: Alammelech refers to a named place in the Hebrew Old Testament. It occurs once, in Joshua 19:26, and is rendered “Alammelech.” Because this word is preserved as a place-name rather than supplied with an explicit definition, its main function is identification: it distinguishes a particular location in the land. The surrounding verse is needed to explain its exact role in that passage; the word itself primarily names the place.

word:hebrew:H4911.explanation: Mâshal means to liken or compare. It can also describe becoming like something else. It may refer to using a proverb or other figurative language.

word:hebrew:H5048.explanation: Neged means in front of, opposite, or over against. It can also refer to a counterpart or mate, as in the helper described as comparable to the man. It may also describe being before someone, as when men sat before him.

word:hebrew:H5130.explanation: Nûwph means to move or shake something back and forth or up and down, including waving it. It is used when a breast is waved before Yahweh as a wave offering.

word:hebrew:H5149.explanation: Nechum is the personal name Nehum, an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H5185.explanation: Nâchêth means descending, or coming down.

word:hebrew:H519.explanation: Amāh means a maid-servant or female slave.

word:hebrew:H5394.explanation: Nâshal means to pluck off or take off. It can describe casting people out from a place. It can also describe something dropping off, as olives do from a tree.

word:hebrew:H5466.explanation: Sadin means a wrapper or shirt, a kind of clothing. It can also refer to fine linen or a sheet.

word:hebrew:H5488.explanation: Suph means a reed, especially papyrus. It can also refer to the Red Sea.

word:hebrew:H5563.explanation: Semadar means a vine blossom or tender grape.

word:hebrew:H5581.explanation: Sisamai is a personal name, identifying a person in the Old Testament genealogy. It is not presented as a general word describing an action, quality, or object. The name occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in 1 Chronicles 2:40, within a family record that connects the person with begetting and genealogy. Its meaning as a name is therefore best understood by the individual it identifies rather than by a separate ordinary-word definition.

word:hebrew:H560.explanation: Amar means to say or speak; it can also mean to command.

word:hebrew:H5615.explanation: Seforah means a number or numeration.

word:hebrew:H5732.explanation: Iddan means a set time or period; it can describe a measured period, such as seven times passing over someone.

word:hebrew:H5747.explanation: Og is the name of a king of Bashan.

word:hebrew:H5839.explanation: Azariah is a personal name, identifying a person rather than describing an action or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in Daniel 2:17, and English Bible renderings preserve it as “Azariah.” Because a personal name identifies someone, its precise significance in that passage depends on the surrounding verse and narrative, rather than on the name alone. Here, the word functions simply as the name of the person being mentioned.

word:hebrew:H5912.explanation: Akan is the name of an Israelite. English Scripture renders this name as Achan.

word:hebrew:H5967.explanation: This Hebrew word means “ribs,” referring to the bones along the sides of the chest. It functions as a noun naming that part of the body. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Daniel 7:5. Because the word appears only there and the surrounding verse text is not included here, its basic meaning can be stated clearly, while its precise significance in that passage depends on the context of Daniel’s vision.

word:hebrew:H6016.explanation: Omer means a sheaf. It can also refer to a dry measure equal to one tenth of an ephah.

word:hebrew:H6225.explanation: ʻAshan means to smoke. It can also describe anger smoking against a person.

word:hebrew:H623.explanation: Asaph is a personal name. It can refer to an Israelite or to the family of an Israelite named Asaph.

word:hebrew:H6290.explanation: Paran names a desert of Arabia.

word:hebrew:H6351.explanation: Pachach means to spread a net. It can also describe people being snared in holes.

word:hebrew:H6423.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to an unspecified person or thing, functioning in English like “such.” It points to someone or something without identifying it by name, so its precise reference comes from the surrounding sentence. The word occurs three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, appearing once each in Ruth, 1 Samuel, and 2 Kings. Its use is therefore limited but consistent: it serves as a general designation when a specific name or identity is not given.

word:hebrew:H6517.explanation: Parur means a skillet, pan, or pot.

word:hebrew:H6562.explanation: This Hebrew word means “break,” expressing an action rather than naming a person or thing. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Daniel 4:27. Its basic sense is focused and direct: “break.” The surrounding verse is needed to determine precisely what is being broken in that occurrence, since the verse text is not included here. Thus, readers should understand this word as describing the action of breaking, without extending it to additional meanings.

word:hebrew:H6719.explanation: The Hebrew word means “hunters,” referring to people who hunt. It is a plural noun, so it identifies more than one person rather than an action or quality. This word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Jeremiah 16:16. Its basic meaning remains focused and concrete: people identified by hunting. The precise force of the word in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H6760.explanation: Tsala means to limp or halt.

word:hebrew:H6801.explanation: Tsânaph means to wrap or roll something around. It can also describe being dressed or attired in clothing.

word:hebrew:H6908.explanation: Qabats means to collect or gather. It can describe people being gathered together.

word:hebrew:H6944.explanation: Qodesh means something sacred or holy. It can refer to a sacred place, as with holy ground and the holy place. It can also describe a sacred thing, such as holy bread.

word:hebrew:H7011.explanation: Qayam means permanent, steadfast, or sure.

word:hebrew:H7165.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “taches,” naming the connecting items used in the tabernacle’s curtain construction. It appears ten times in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, all in Exodus, especially in instructions for joining and arranging the tabernacle curtains. The word therefore identifies a physical component of the sanctuary’s structure rather than an action, quality, or person. Its use is concentrated in the account of building the tabernacle and its furnishings. References include Exodus 26:6, 26:11, 26:33, 35:11, 36:13, and 36:18.

word:hebrew:H717.explanation: Arâh means to pluck. It can also describe gathering, as when myrrh is gathered.

word:hebrew:H7297.explanation: Râhâh means to fear or be afraid.

word:hebrew:H7338.explanation: Rachab means width or breadth. It can also describe a broad place.

word:hebrew:H7433.explanation: Ramoth-Gilead is the name of a place east of the Jordan.

word:hebrew:H762.explanation: Aramith means in Aramaic, referring to the Syrian language or tongue.

word:hebrew:H7635.explanation: Shabiyl means a track or passageway, such as a path or way.

word:hebrew:H7680.explanation: Sega means to increase, grow, or multiply.

word:hebrew:H7727.explanation: Shobab is a personal name used for two Israelites.

word:hebrew:H7752.explanation: Shote means a lash, literally or figuratively, including a whip or scourge.

word:hebrew:H7806.explanation: The word means “twined,” describing material or fabric made by strands being joined together. In its Hebrew Old Testament use, it refers to the construction of the tabernacle and its furnishings, including curtains, screens, hangings, and priestly clothing. It occurs 21 times, all in Exodus, so its normal sense is tied to prepared materials used in the sanctuary. Its precise force in any one verse comes from the object it describes.

word:hebrew:H8061.explanation: Shemida is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Shemida” in the Old Testament. It identifies the same named person in three genealogical passages: Numbers 26:32, Joshua 17:2, and 1 Chronicles 7:19. These occurrences connect the name with family and tribal records, rather than presenting it as a common word describing an action, quality, or object. The available passages preserve the name’s identification, but do not provide a separate lexical definition or explain its underlying name meaning.

word:hebrew:H8083.explanation: Shemoneh means eight, a cardinal number. It appears in counted quantities, including eight hundred years and eight boards.

word:hebrew:H8128.explanation: Shen means a tooth. In Scripture, it is rendered as “teeth” when referring to more than one.

word:hebrew:H8164.explanation: Sa'iyr means a shower or small rain.

word:hebrew:H8300.explanation: Sarid means a survivor, someone who remains alive.

word:hebrew:H8379.explanation: Ta'avah means a limit or full extent—the utmost bound.

word:hebrew:H8429.explanation: Tᵉvahh means to be amazed or alarmed.

word:hebrew:H8573.explanation: Tenuphah means a wave offering—the appointed waving of a sacrificial offering before Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H8591.explanation: Ta'a means to cheat or deceive. It can also describe misuse.

word:hebrew:H8656.explanation: Tirtsah is a place name and also the name of a woman. It refers to a place in one passage and to one of Zelophehad’s daughters in another.

word:hebrew:H898.explanation: Bagad means to deal deceitfully or treacherously—to act unfaithfully toward another.

word:hebrew:H982.explanation: Batach means to trust or place confidence in someone or something. It may describe trusting in Yahweh or trusting in a bow.
